description: Schmitt trigger 4.5V~5.5V 8 1 8.5ns@5V,50pF TSSOP-20 Buffers, Drivers, Receivers, Transceivers RoHS

provenance.pins: datasheet section 5.1 Pinning, D/SOT163-1 (SO20) diagram Supply range 4.5-5.5 V from p.2 Recommended Operating Conditions.

notes: SCOPE CHANGED by the move to a differential pair. The two WS2812 data lines now leave the controller as differential pairs from MAX3485 transceivers driven straight off 3.3 V GPIOs, so the level shifting for them has moved to the converter boards. The only 5 V logic left on the controller is the single status-LED chain. An octal buffer for one channel is overkill - a single-gate HCT buffer would do, though none surfaced in the JLCPCB assembly catalogue, so the octal may simply stay as the available option.
HCT inputs have TTL thresholds (~1.5 V), so a 3.3 V GPIO drives them as a valid high, and the output swings to the 5 V rail. Plain HC would not work: its threshold is 0.7 x VCC = 3.5 V.

Octal, and this design uses ONE channel: A0/Y0 carry the status LED chain. The other seven inputs are tied to GND and their outputs left open. The two module data channels went to MAX3485 differential drivers, so no 5 V logic is left on them.

Supply range 4.5-5.5 V. From the TPS54360B's Eq. 1 with the real inductor DCR the rail is 4.56 V at a 4.75 V bus on a typical converter - 0.06 V over the floor - and 4.48 V at the converter's applicable worst-case on-resistance, about 20 mV UNDER it. See C524806. Tolerable only because this part drives the status LED chain: a marginal rail during the few seconds of the 5 V phase means the indicators may misbehave before negotiation, not that the board fails to start.
TERMINOLOGY: called a differential pair in the design docs. RS-485 line levels, but no RS-485 connector convention - the pair runs over two poles of a picoMAX next to power and ground.
SETTLED as U9 in the BOM: it drives the status chain only, one channel of eight. Oversized but it is what the assembly catalogue offers.

NOT DELETABLE BY ANY LED CHOICE. Three SK6812 variants were compared (C5149201, C2909058, C2890041) and every one wants VIH >= 0.6-0.65 x VDD, i.e. 3.0-3.25 V on a 5 V rail; the fitted SK6812-EC20 is the most permissive at 0.6 x VDD = 3.00 V, and the ESP32-C6's guaranteed V_OH of 0.8 x 3.3 = 2.64 V still does not reach it. Even the most permissive is out of reach.
designVerdict: SELECTED as U9 - the SK6812 status chain needs 5 V logic from a 3.3 V GPIO. Oversized (octal, one channel used) but the cheapest available part that does the level shift.

rules.note: active-low output enable; tie to GND or the buffer never drives.
the second active-low output enable - both halves must be enabled.
